newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen slightly softer at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen slightly softer at open.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open steady to slightly softer on Tuesday, taking their cues from the bond market as the second quarter employment cost index came in as forecast.
The Labor Department reported the employment cost index rose 0.8 percent in the second quarter, as forecast, compared with a 0.6 percent rise the previous quarter.
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index, which was higher before the release of the data, slipped 3.55 points to 940.10.
The long bond, which was robust yesterday, eased 8/32 to yield 6.42 percent.

"I thought the employment cost report would cause a more positive reaction in stocks and bonds," Alfred Kugel, Stein Roe & Farnham senior investment strategist, said. "Maybe a lot of good news has already been priced into markets."
Financial markets would also digest news of a historic accord which was hammered out between President Clinton and Republicans to balance the federal budget and cut taxes.
Some analysts said the pact would be a positive factor in markets. Others said it had already been priced into stocks.
